glossary.definition: Key (primary source hitting the subject front at an angle), fill (opposite the key, lifting shadow detail) and backlight/rim (from behind, higher than the subject, separating it from the background and making the frame feel three-dimensional rather than flat) [FACT — StudioBinder three-point + backlight guides, riverside.com].

Light designed to imitate a plausible in-world source (window sun, lamp, moonlight) even when the fixture creating it is off-screen; often used to accentuate practicals [FACT — StudioBinder, FilmDaft]. Its role as the anti-AI-look keystone is tagged ESTIMATE (high confidence; unmotivated glow is a recognized CG/AI tell).

Visible in-frame light sources — table lamp, neon sign, chandelier, sconce, candles — that justify the lighting, add depth and separation, and carry narrative information [FACT — StudioBinder practical-lighting].

Black flag or fabric on the side opposite the key that ABSORBS light, deepening shadows; increases contrast, adds mood, sculpts faces; described as one of the most-used cinematic techniques especially with a soft key [FACT — Indie Cinema Academy, ISO1200].

The stop difference between the lit and shadow side of a face; high-key minimizes it toward 1:1 (bright, few shadows), low-key runs it high (e.g. 8:1) for deep chiaroscuro shadows [FACT — Wikipedia high/low-key excerpts, wolfcrow, Backstage].

Shortly after sunrise / before sunset: light is redder, softer, strongly directional with long elegant shadows; the atmosphere scatters blue wavelengths out and 'the sky becomes an enormous soft-box lighting instrument' (UCLA's William McDonald). Duration varies — Nestor Almendros called 'hour' a euphemism, sometimes ~15 minutes [FACT — Wikipedia excerpt, Backstage, NFI].

Sun below the horizon before sunrise/after sunset; entirely indirect light, deep saturated blue, no sharp shadows; serene, moody, expensive-nocturne feel [FACT — Wikipedia + remote-expeditions excerpts].

The automotive-stage principle: light the REFLECTIONS, not the object — very large white surfaces (reported up to ~30x60 ft) are lit and reflected into the paintwork, a silk above smooths the curves, because specular reflections of large sources define glossy shape [ESTIMATE — medium-high confidence: primary ASC source located but 403-blocked, reconstructed from excerpts plus No Film School / Lightmap / Mammoth London].

One small living element per quiet-luxury shot — curtain moving, steam rising, a glass sweating — that makes an otherwise still frame feel photographed and real; paired with 'barely there' camera motion [FACT-1src — Upscale Living quiet-luxury piece + luxury-brand-film guides].

The minimum realism clause of every prompt: 'natural motivated lighting, realistic skin texture, film grain, no artificial smoothness' plus one living micro-detail — the floor below which luxury footage reads as generated [ESTIMATE — craft mapping built on the sourced motivated-lighting and micro-detail claims; effectiveness untested until the L5 credit run].

nodes.definition: Command the baseline setup every other recipe modifies: three-point lighting. The key is the primary source, hitting the subject's front at an angle; the fill sits opposite the key and lifts shadow detail; the backlight/rim comes from behind and higher than the subject, separating it from the background and 'making a frame feel three-dimensional rather than flat' [FACT — StudioBinder three-point + backlight guides, riverside.com]. For luxury persona shots the rim is the load-bearing element — separation is what reads as produced rather than flat — and the fill level is the dial the contrast-ratio node turns. Every mood recipe in this KB is a named deviation from this triangle: quiet luxury deletes the artificial key for a window, night luxe hands the key to practicals, negative fill replaces added fill with subtraction.

nodes.definition: Set the contrast key of every scene. The lighting contrast ratio is the stop difference between the lit and shadow side of a face. High-key minimizes the ratio, approaching 1:1 — bright, low-contrast, few shadows (sitcoms, La La Land). Low-key uses a high ratio, e.g. 8:1 — deep shadows, chiaroscuro (Whiplash, Fincher, The Batman) [FACT — Wikipedia high/low-key excerpts, wolfcrow, Backstage]. The ratio is the single number that most changes a frame's mood: the same set at 1:1 reads open and commercial, at 8:1 it reads dramatic and expensive. Luxury work in this KB defaults toward controlled contrast (moderate-to-low-key) because flat high-key is also the plastic AI-render look, but the ratio is chosen per scene mood, not globally.

nodes.definition: Hold the definition that anchors the whole KB: motivated lighting is light designed to imitate a plausible in-world source — window sun, a lamp, moonlight — even when the fixture actually creating it is off-screen; it is often used to accentuate practicals [FACT — StudioBinder motivated-lighting, FilmDaft]. The discipline is directional: first name the world's source, then shape the light to look like that source produced it. A motivated frame answers 'where is that light coming from?' with something visible or plausibly just out of frame; an unmotivated frame answers with 'the lighting rig' or, in generation, 'the model's prior'. This node carries only the FACT definition; the anti-AI keystone application is its own node so its ESTIMATE tag stays separate.

nodes.definition: Deploy practicals — visible in-frame sources: table lamp, neon sign, chandelier, sconce, candles. They justify the lighting, add depth and separation, and carry narrative information [FACT — StudioBinder practical-lighting]. For AI generation practicals are doubly valuable: they are the cheapest way to make a frame's light self-motivating (the source is literally in shot, so no off-screen plausibility argument is needed), and they give the model a concrete object to render the glow around, which anchors light direction and color. A practical named in the prompt ('lit by the warm table lamp at frame right') simultaneously sets source, direction, warmth and a set-dressing element. The risk is exposure: a practical that blows out becomes its own unmotivated-looking bloom.

nodes.definition: Sculpt by subtraction: negative fill is black flag or fabric placed on the side opposite the key that ABSORBS light, deepening shadows; it increases contrast, adds mood and sculpts faces, and is described as one of the most-used cinematic techniques especially with a soft key [FACT — Indie Cinema Academy, ISO1200]. In prompt terms negative fill translates not as equipment but as its visible result: 'one side of the face falling into deep shadow, high contrast soft light, moody chiaroscuro'. It is the mechanical partner of the low-key ratio choice — the way a soft, flattering key still yields deep-shadow drama — and the darkness it creates is also what glossy metal needs to reflect (feeding the specular-transfer node). Its hazard is over-subtraction: a shadow side gone fully black loses the sculpt it was meant to create.

conflict_axes.description: Practicals justify light and dress the frame, but the quiet-luxury register demands minimal additions and the cleanest lines — lamps everywhere break the restraint.
poles: let practicals carry and dress the frame
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: register decides: night-luxe frames want visible warm practicals; daylight quiet-luxury wants the window alone with 'lit only by' enforced

conflict_axes.name: per_clip_best_light_vs_cross_seam_continuity
conflict_axes.description: Each clip generates best when its prompt is free to chase its own most flattering light, but stitched seams need both keyframes locked to one recipe.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: continuity wins at every seam; per-clip optimization is allowed only in the clip's interior, never at its boundary frames

conflict_axes.name: estimate_recipes_vs_fact_only_confidence
conflict_axes.description: The most commercially valuable signatures (car specular, watch transfer, night-luxe) are ESTIMATE-tagged, while the safest FACT claims are generic definitions — value and verification pull apart.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use ESTIMATE signatures but price the risk: validate on cheap stills before hero spend, carry the tag in every downstream document, and log outcomes to upgrade or demote

conflict_axes.name: descriptor_density_vs_prompt_clarity
conflict_axes.description: Lighting is the top lever, tempting authors to stack every descriptor; but a prompt carrying seven lighting ideas gives the model contradictions and muddies the mood.
poles: one recipe, few clauses, clean read
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: one recipe per shot: the scene's recipe plus the floor and nothing else; extra lighting ideas mean the shot list needs another shot, not a longer prompt

conflict_axes.name: shadow_depth_vs_subject_legibility
conflict_axes.description: Negative fill and low-key ratios buy expensive darkness, but shadow that swallows the face or product loses the very subject the frame sells.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: shadow may take everything except the subject's defining edge: faces keep their far-edge sculpt, products keep their gradient highlight; if either vanishes, lift the shadow one step

edge_cases.description: The ASC car-lighting article — the reflection principle's primary source — is 403-blocked, so the KB's highest-value product signature rests on reconstructed excerpts
edge_cases.trigger: anyone tries to quote the light-the-reflections principle as verified FACT in a downstream document or brief
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the ESTIMATE (medium-high) tag and the named egress blocker everywhere the principle travels; re-verify and upgrade when theasc.com becomes reachable

edge_cases.description: The 'golden hour' label names a state Almendros said can last ~15 minutes, so two generations of the same scene land at visibly different sun heights
edge_cases.trigger: a golden-hour scene spans multiple clips or a clip is regenerated after a QC failure
edge_cases.mitigation: pin sun height, shadow length and warmth in explicit words in every prompt of the scene rather than trusting the two-word label

edge_cases.description: A generated frame carries an attractive glow no in-world source can explain — the recognized CG/AI tell
edge_cases.trigger: the model invents ambient or rim light beyond the named sources, especially in interiors
edge_cases.mitigation: fail the frame at the motivation check regardless of beauty; regenerate with the source named harder ('lit only by...') and the glow negated

edge_cases.description: A blue-hour prompt collapses into generic night — black sky, sodium streetlights — losing the saturated indigo the register depends on
edge_cases.trigger: the prompt says 'evening' or 'dusk' instead of naming the deep indigo ambient explicitly
edge_cases.mitigation: always use recipe (6)'s full wording — 'blue hour, deep indigo ambient light, no direct sun' — and QC for the blue cast specifically

edge_cases.description: The watch/jewelry recipe is two ESTIMATE links deep (blocked ASC parent + unfetched transfer), making it the weakest-sourced signature in the KB
edge_cases.trigger: a hero watch or jewelry shot is scheduled before any test generation has validated the gradient-highlight recipe
edge_cases.mitigation: validate the recipe on cheap test stills first; treat failures as hypothesis data and fall back to simple soft-source product lighting if the transfer does not hold

edge_cases.description: The one living micro-detail renders too violently — a curtain whipping, steam billowing — turning quiet luxury into weather drama
edge_cases.trigger: the model amplifies the named micro-motion beyond the 'barely there' register
edge_cases.mitigation: qualify the detail's magnitude in the prompt ('stirring slightly', 'a thin wisp') and swap to a gentler detail type if the model keeps overdoing it

edge_cases.description: A high-key request produces the flat, shadowless, plastic render look — technically compliant, commercially dead
edge_cases.trigger: a bright daytime mood is prompted without a contrast guard, minimizing the ratio toward 1:1
edge_cases.mitigation: default luxury scenes to controlled contrast; when high-key is truly wanted, keep directional shape ('soft directional daylight') and the texture floor to avoid flatness

edge_cases.description: Two seam keyframes were prompted with paraphrased rather than identical recipe text and render at different brightness/warmth, exposing the cut
edge_cases.trigger: a prompt author rewrites the recipe from memory for the second keyframe of a seam pair
edge_cases.mitigation: copy recipe strings verbatim between seam-pair prompts and have the gate compare the pair before video generation spends credits

edge_cases.description: A practical blows out into a white halo — the justifying source itself becomes the unmotivated-looking bloom
edge_cases.trigger: a neon sign, chandelier or lamp is rendered heavily overexposed against a dark frame
edge_cases.mitigation: describe the practical's legible state ('a legible pink neon tube', 'warm lamp glow, not blown out') and fail frames where the source's shape is lost

edge_cases.description: Every phrase in the recipe table is untested per model until the L5 credit run — the whole prompt layer is hypothesis, not validated control
edge_cases.trigger: production planning treats the mapping table as proven and skips the still-image validation pass
edge_cases.mitigation: run the first credit budget as an explicit recipe A/B on stills, log per-phrase outcomes through the QC gate, and only then lock the table for production

edge_cases.description: A chosen Higgsfield preset's built-in lighting language (e.g. SUMMER HAZE's lomo light leaks) contradicts the scene's recipe, and the preset's actual behavior beyond its description is unknown
edge_cases.trigger: a preset is selected for its subject or motion while its description names a conflicting light style
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the adopt-or-avoid rule: either make the preset's lighting language the scene's recipe or pick another preset; never fight a preset with a contradicting recipe

edge_cases.description: Chiaroscuro on a face at close-up loses the shadow-side edge entirely, reading as underexposure instead of sculpt
edge_cases.trigger: negative-fill result language is pushed ('deep shadow') without preserving the far-edge detail
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the shadow-depth-vs-legibility rule: the subject's defining edge must survive; if it vanishes, lift the shadow one step and regenerate

workflow.action: Fix the keystone veto for the whole reel: every light must be justifiable by an in-world source
workflow.description: State the justify-or-delete rule and its honesty split (definition FACT, anti-AI linkage ESTIMATE) in the production brief before any prompt is written
workflow.artifact: lighting keystone clause in the reel brief
workflow.gate: the veto rule and its FACT/ESTIMATE split are stated verbatim in the brief

workflow.action: Declare each scene's contrast key and mood register
workflow.description: Choose high-key vs low-key per scene with the stop-difference definition in hand, defaulting luxury scenes to controlled contrast
workflow.gate: every scene has a named ratio register with a one-line mood justification

workflow.action: Assign the natural-light window per exterior scene
workflow.description: Choose golden hour, blue hour or neutral day per scene, pinning sun-state descriptors wherever a scene spans clips
workflow.artifact: natural-light schedule with pinned sun states
workflow.gate: no multi-clip scene relies on a bare 'golden hour'/'blue hour' label

workflow.action: Select the luxury signature per subject
workflow.description: Map each subject to its signature: gloss products to reflection lighting, interiors to window quiet-luxury, night scenes to low-key practicals, aspirational exteriors to golden rim
workflow.gate: every shot has exactly one signature and each ESTIMATE-tagged signature is marked for still validation

workflow.action: Write the lighting recipe as the leading clause of every prompt
workflow.description: Place the scene's recipe text first per the Veo most-impactful-lever excerpt, using the sourced descriptor vocabulary
workflow.gate: no prompt buries its lighting clause behind camera or wardrobe text

workflow.action: Append the anti-AI floor plus one living micro-detail to every prompt
workflow.description: Add the floor clause and exactly one quiet micro-detail, then lint every prompt for both
workflow.gate: every prompt contains the floor clause, a named in-world source, and exactly one micro-detail

workflow.action: Duplicate recipes verbatim across seam keyframe pairs
workflow.description: Copy the identical recipe string into the end-keyframe prompt of clip N and start-keyframe prompt of clip N+1 for every seam
workflow.gate: a string comparison shows byte-identical recipe text within every seam pair

workflow.action: Reconcile recipes with any Higgsfield preset in use
workflow.description: Read each chosen preset's description against the recipe and apply adopt-or-avoid; log the open Camera-Controls UNKNOWN where relevant
workflow.gate: no shot pairs a preset with a recipe its description contradicts

workflow.action: Generate validation stills for every ESTIMATE-tagged recipe before hero video spend
workflow.description: Run cheap still generations for car specular, watch transfer and night-luxe recipes and judge them against their nodes' acceptance descriptions
workflow.artifact: still-validation contact sheet with pass/fail per recipe
workflow.gate: every ESTIMATE recipe has at least one passing still or a documented fallback

workflow.action: Run the five-check lighting QC gate on all stills and clips
workflow.description: Check motivation, recipe match, floor, seam pairs and the honesty log in order; regenerate failures with the specific clause strengthened
workflow.gate: every accepted frame passed all five checks and every failure names its failed check

workflow.action: Feed the QC failure log back into the recipe table after the credit run
workflow.description: Upgrade, demote or rewrite recipes using the logged per-phrase outcomes, replacing untested-ESTIMATE tags with observed results
workflow.artifact: revised recipe table with evidence annotations
workflow.gate: every recipe's tag reflects the latest run evidence, none silently upgraded

dominance_rules.rule: When any stylization conflicts with the motivated-realism floor, the floor wins
dominance_rules.rationale: the reel's premise is photographed-not-generated; one unmotivated glow costs more than any mood gain, per the keystone's recognized-AI-tell basis
dominance_rules.trigger: a recipe, preset or reviewer pushes a look that violates 'natural motivated lighting' or 'no artificial smoothness'
dominance_rules.action: revise the stylization to motivated means or drop it; never edit the floor clause

dominance_rules.rule: The research file's honesty tag dominates every downstream restatement
dominance_rules.rationale: the ASC source was 403-blocked, quiet-luxury is FACT-1src, the recipe table is untested — upgrading any of these invents certainty the pipeline does not have
dominance_rules.trigger: a claim from this KB is quoted in a brief, prompt doc or report
dominance_rules.action: carry FACT/FACT-1src/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN exactly as tagged; upgrades require a fetched source or logged run evidence

dominance_rules.rule: For specular subjects, the reflection principle dominates the aim-light-at-it instinct
dominance_rules.rationale: specular surfaces show their environment: large reflected sources define gloss shape, point sources produce the plastic look — carried at ESTIMATE but still the best available guidance
dominance_rules.trigger: a car, watch or glossy product shot is being lit or prompted
dominance_rules.action: light/describe the reflections (large soft gliding highlights, dark edge reflections), not the object, and validate on stills given the ESTIMATE tag

dominance_rules.rationale: matching texture, color and brightness across the cut is what sells the illusion; a prettier clip that breaks its seam costs the whole reel
dominance_rules.trigger: a clip regeneration or per-clip optimization would change light at a seam boundary frame
dominance_rules.action: hold the seam pair's identical recipe and sun state; optimize only the clip interior

dominance_rules.rule: Controlled contrast dominates high-key for luxury moods by default
dominance_rules.rationale: flat near-1:1 light is both the sitcom register and the plastic AI-render adjacency; the sourced luxury signatures are all contrast-carrying
dominance_rules.trigger: a scene's ratio is being declared without a strong high-key justification
dominance_rules.action: default to a directional, shadow-carrying register and demand explicit justification for any 1:1 look

dominance_rules.rule: One recipe per shot dominates descriptor stacking
dominance_rules.rationale: stacked lighting ideas hand the model contradictions; the recipe plus the floor is the whole lighting budget of a prompt
dominance_rules.trigger: a prompt draft carries clauses from more than one recipe
dominance_rules.action: cut to the scene's single recipe plus floor; move surplus ideas to a new shot in the list

dominance_rules.rule: A named in-world source dominates abstract mood adjectives in prompt text
dominance_rules.rationale: 'lit by the window at frame left' is checkable against the frame and satisfies the keystone; 'beautiful cinematic lighting' is neither
dominance_rules.trigger: a prompt describes light quality without naming where it comes from
dominance_rules.action: rewrite the clause around a named source (window, lamp, sun, practical) before generation

dominance_rules.rule: The QC gate's motivation check dominates schedule pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: shipping one sourceless-glow frame undermines the reel's entire photographed premise; regeneration cost is bounded, the tell's cost is not
dominance_rules.trigger: a deadline tempts acceptance of an attractive frame that fails the motivation check
dominance_rules.action: regenerate with the source named harder; the gate does not pass exceptions

dominance_rules.rule: Preset lighting language dominates a contradicting recipe when a preset is used
dominance_rules.rationale: the preset chain's behavior beyond its description is unknown; fighting its built-in look wastes credits on a battle the prompt may not win
dominance_rules.trigger: a chosen preset's description names a light style different from the scene's recipe
dominance_rules.action: adopt the preset's lighting language as the scene recipe or switch presets; never run both

anti_rework_rules.rule: Lock each scene's recipe and contrast key before writing any keyframe prompt
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regenerating whole seam pairs because the two keyframes were authored under different lighting assumptions

anti_rework_rules.rule: Copy recipe strings verbatim into both prompts of every seam pair before generation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a paraphrase-induced brightness/warmth jump discovered only after both clips spent video credits

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the in-world source in every prompt before it reaches the queue
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rounds of unmotivated-glow regenerations that a one-line source clause would have avoided

anti_rework_rules.rule: Validate every ESTIMATE-tagged recipe (car specular, watch transfer, night-luxe) on cheap stills before any hero video spend
anti_rework_rules.prevents: burning the hero budget on a two-ESTIMATE-deep recipe the chosen model turns out to ignore

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read a preset's lighting description and apply adopt-or-avoid before pairing it with a scene
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering mid-run that the preset's built-in look (light leaks, floodlights) fights the recipe and every clip needs redoing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pin sun-state descriptors for any golden/blue-hour scene that spans clips before generating the first clip
anti_rework_rules.prevents: sun-height drift across clips that forces regenerating the whole scene to a common state

anti_rework_rules.rule: Include the anti-AI floor and the single micro-detail in the first generation, never as a patch pass
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a second full generation round because realism clauses were deferred to 'fix it later'

anti_rework_rules.rule: Log every QC failure with its failed check and phrase from the first credit run onward
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-discovering which lighting phrases work on each model in every subsequent production cycle

iteration_protocol.trigger: the QC gate fails a frame on the motivation check (sourceless glow)
iteration_protocol.action: strengthen the source clause ('lit only by...'), negate the glow, regenerate, and log the failing phrase

iteration_protocol.trigger: a seam pair renders with visible brightness/color mismatch despite identical recipe text
iteration_protocol.action: pin additional state descriptors (sun height, warmth, exposure anchors) in both prompts, regenerate the cheaper keyframe first, and record the variance as model behavior

iteration_protocol.trigger: the L5 credit run produces per-phrase effectiveness data for the recipe table
iteration_protocol.action: upgrade recipes that held, rewrite or demote those that failed, and replace the table-wide untested-ESTIMATE tag with per-recipe evidence annotations

iteration_protocol.trigger: theasc.com becomes fetchable and the car-reflection article can be read in full
iteration_protocol.action: verify the light-the-reflections reconstruction against the primary text and upgrade or correct the ESTIMATE tag on the car and watch nodes

iteration_protocol.trigger: the Higgsfield-surface enumeration lands and resolves the Camera-Controls-to-MCP mapping UNKNOWN
iteration_protocol.action: reconcile the recipe and preset-alignment guidance with the enumerated parameters and retire the named blocker

iteration_protocol.trigger: accepted footage still reads generated despite passing the motivation check
iteration_protocol.action: audit the non-motivation floor clauses (texture, smoothness, micro-detail magnitude), strengthen the weakest, and note that the keystone linkage is ESTIMATE — necessary but evidently not sufficient

iteration_protocol.trigger: a second independent source corroborates or contradicts a FACT-1src claim (quiet-luxury formula, micro-detail rule)
iteration_protocol.action: upgrade the tag to FACT on corroboration or revise the node on contradiction, and propagate the change to the recipe table

iteration_protocol.trigger: night-luxe or chiaroscuro frames repeatedly read underexposed rather than low-key
iteration_protocol.action: apply the legibility rule (subject's defining edge must survive), lift shadow one step in the recipe wording, and re-declare the scene's ratio if needed

priority_rationale: The foundations come first because everything else is defined against them: the three-point triangle and contrast ratio give every recipe its geometry and mood dial, the motivated-lighting definition anchors the keystone, and the Veo lever ranking justifies putting lighting first in prompts at all; the craft tools (practicals, negative fill) and natural-light registers (golden, blue) then supply the sourced ingredients; the anti-AI keystone and micro-detail convert those into the reel's realism discipline; the luxury signatures (reflections-not-object, window quiet-luxury, golden rim, night luxe) apply the ingredients to the vertical's actual subjects at their honest ESTIMATE/FACT-1src tags; the prompt-translation layer (vocabulary, recipe table, floor, seam continuity, preset alignment) renders it all as testable prompt text; and the QC gate comes last because it composes every upstream rule into the accept/regenerate verdict and generates the evidence that will retire the untested tags.
